newsitem.title: JAPAN: NKorea slams U.S. for planned arms sales to South.
newsitem.headline: NKorea slams U.S. for planned arms sales to South.

text.p: North Korea resumed its verbal attacks on Saturday, denouncing a planned arms sale by the United States to South Korea as a U.S. move to "unleash a war" against Pyongyang.
"The Korean Peninsula is now in an unpredictable situation owing to the U.S. military reinforcement and moves to provoke a war," said the Rodong Sinmun, mouthpiece of North Korea's ruling party.

"If the U.S. war maniacs foolishly ignite a war of aggression on the DPRK (North Korea), our people and people's army will take a merciless and decisive counterattack," the newspaper said in a commentary carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).
KCNA said in the report, monitored in Tokyo, that the United States has planned to sell more than 1,060 "stinger" missiles and 200 launchers to South Korea.
In a separate report on Saturday, KCNA carried comments by the nation's leader Kim Jong-il, who warned that "imperialists" gave aid as a means of dominating other countries.
"The imperialists' 'aid' to other countries is a noose with which to further plunder and subjugate them," KCNA quoted Kim to say in his writing published on Thursday.
"Illusions about imperialism as well as fear of it must be eliminated. Aggression and plunder constitute the nature of imperialism," Kim wrote.
The reports follow warnings from North Korea earlier this week that the armed forces were ready for a "final battle" with the United States and South Korea.

On Wednesday, a North Korean military spokesman warned that the recent South Korean amphibious exercises on islands near the North, as well as some U.S. exercises, showed that Seoul and Washington were set to strike while the famine-stricken North was weak.
North Korea had recently stepped up its verbal attack on South Korea and the United States in what analysts said was a distorted way of securing closer ties with Washington.
After a series of war threats in 1994, North Korea won its game of diplomatic brinkmanship and persuaded the United States to sit at a table for face-to-face talks.
